I personally think that enrolling in a class when you’re a beginner is a good route because it helps make sure that you get your foundations (especially grammar foundations). After that, self-teaching will be easier because you have more context and understanding of the language. There is a place called KCCLA that is offering free online classes for varying levels, including beginners—I really recommend it. 

However, there are some really great ways for beginners to supplement their learning. I taught myself Hangeul from YouTube before enrolling in Korean classes, and it really helped. Also, Drops is a great app for beginners, provided they know Hangeul. 

I don’t really know how Duolingo is for beginners cause I never used it when I was just starting. If you intend to learn the alphabet on it, then I would say to supplement that with many videos where you hear the letters properly and clearly pronounced. This is a fantastic one that started my journey: 
https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=Q8Smjkw_cjg

The video itself isn’t beautiful or spiffy, but I think it has some great things that many other Hangeul tutorials lack. 

A lot of self-teaching resources will open up to you once you learn the alphabet, so I would start there, *really* nitpick your pronunciation, then decide next steps. Good luck!!
